raw_case_text:
A 35-year-old man was admitted at the oculistic emergency room for a right exophthalmos accompanied with severe pain, periorbital swelling, redness, and mucopurulent discharge. The patient, HIV and HCV positive for 11 years, had a history of drug and alcohol addiction, including habitual marijuana smoking. Clinical examination revealed severe nonreducible exophthalmos with bulb dislocated medially and inferiorly, associated with eyelid chemosis and decreased vision in the right eye (1/10). The motility of the globe in all gazes was restricted by mechanical proptosis. Fundus examination revealed optic disc swelling associated with venous congestion. A brain MRI was performed in order to evaluate the involvement of the orbit and the brain. The examination showed an intraorbital mass that was inhomogeneously hypointense on T2-weighted images and hypointense on T1-weighted images and showed intense and inhomogeneous contrast enhancement. The mass was located in the lateral orbit cavity extending to the ethmoid and maxillary sinuses, with bony destruction, encasing and displacing the medial rectus and superior oblique muscles, optic nerve, ocular globe, and vascular structures (Figure 1).
On the basis of these findings and considering patient's history of HIV related diseases and drug addiction, few diagnosis have been hypothesized that included neoplastic diseases, e.g., lymphoma, and infections, in particular mycotic origin, such as aspergillosis, considering the known association with marijuana smoking. Prior to beginning any treatment, the patient was subjected to a biopsy of the orbital mass. At histology H&E stain of the tumor showed a monomorphic proliferation of plasmablastic cells that was suggestive of plasmablastic lymphoma. The patient died within a week following diagnosis for a heart attack, even before further treatment could be initiated.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 35-year-old male presenting with acute painful right eye protrusion, periorbital swelling, redness, and mucopurulent discharge.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented to the ophthalmology emergency department with rapid-onset right-sided proptosis accompanied by severe orbital pain, periorbital erythema, edema, mucopurulent ocular discharge, and acute visual loss. He reported a multi-year history of chronic substance dependence.
subjective.past_medical_history: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection diagnosed 11 years prior; chronic substance abuse and alcohol addiction, including heavy marijuana smoking.
subjective.review_of_systems: Severe right orbital pain, decreased vision, mucopurulent ocular discharge; denies fever, chills, contralateral eye symptoms, focal limb weakness, or chronic cough.

objective.physical_examination: Ophthalmologic examination (right eye): Severe, non-reducible proptosis with medial and inferior globe displacement; marked conjunctival chemosis and periorbital edema; visual acuity reduced to 1/10; extraocular motility severely restricted in all fields of gaze due to mechanical proptosis. Funduscopy (right eye): Marked optic disc edema with prominent retinal venous engorgement. Left eye: Unremarkable.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain and orbital contrast-enhanced MRI: Large, aggressive, destructive intraorbital mass within the lateral orbit extending into the adjacent ethmoid and maxillary sinuses with cortical bone destruction; mass appeared hypointense on T1-weighted images, heterogeneously hypointense on T2-weighted images, with intense, heterogeneous contrast enhancement, causing encasement and displacement of the optic nerve, medial rectus muscle, superior oblique muscle, and globe. Histopathology of orbital mass biopsy: Monomorphic proliferation of atypical plasmablastic cells with brisk mitotic activity and nuclear pleomorphism, consistent with plasmablastic lymphoma.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Advanced HIV-associated plasmablastic lymphoma (PBL) of the right orbit with ethmoid/maxillary sinus invasion and optic nerve compression, in an HIV- and HCV-seropositive patient; fungal orbital cellulitis/aspergillosis and bacterial orbital abscess were ruled out.
Plan & Outcome: Biopsy of the orbital tumor confirmed high-grade plasmablastic neoplasia. Before systemic chemotherapy or local radiation could be initiated, the patient suffered an acute fatal myocardial infarction and expired within one week of tissue diagnosis.
